topic: Why Another Textbook in Process Dynamics and Control?
title: Why Another Textbook in Process Dynamics and Control?
session_title: In Honor of Professor James B. Rawlings, the 2024 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award (Invited Talks)
abstract: A departure from the classical approach in teaching process dynamics and control, with a model-based approach entirely in the time domain, that underscores the foundations of feedback control and provides a common framework for analysis and design from PID to MPC for chemical and biological processes.

topic: Data-Driven and Physics-Aware Reduced-Order Modeling of Systems with Chaotic Dynamics
title: Data-Driven and Physics-Aware Reduced-Order Modeling of Systems with Chaotic Dynamics
session_title: In Honor of Professor James B. Rawlings, the 2024 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award (Invited Talks)
abstract: Jim Rawlings is an inspiring member of the Chemical Engineering community and I'm proud to call him my colleague, coauthor and friend. This presentation will describe work from my research group on modeling and control of complex nonlinear dynamical systems using methods from machine learning, as well as some reminiscences about my interactions with Jim during his time at Wisconsin.

title: Baby Neural Operators
session_title: In Honor of Professor James B. Rawlings, the 2024 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award (Invited Talks)
abstract: In the 2000 years the Equation-Free approach for multiscale simulations used system identification of local, small space-time patch microscopic simulations, to perform macroscopic modeling tasks. We revisit these algorithms using now small ("baby") local neural operator-based identification as the building block of macroscopic algorithms.

topic: My Learnings from Jim Rawlings about Teaching, Research, ...and Life
title: My Learnings from Jim Rawlings about Teaching, Research, ...and Life
session_title: In Honor of Professor James B. Rawlings, the 2024 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award (Invited Talks)
abstract: In this talk I will describe a subset of lessons I have learned from Jim Rawlings about teaching (reaction engineering and process control), research (how I should have been thinking about modeling), and other topics. These lessons are small anecdotes from Jim's broad, impactful and successful career as an educator.

title: A Journey through the Intersection of Scheduling and Feedback
session_title: In Honor of Professor James B. Rawlings, the 2024 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award (Invited Talks)
abstract: We will discuss how approaching scheduling problems as problems with recourse and feedback, sheds new light on the formulation and solution of the corresponding optimization problems.
